column1: # One line per case where hashpipe's `-c` reader cannot parse the vector as the
# entry stores it, and the type's own serialization has to be supplied. john
# writes RVARY as "$rvary$<hex>" where mdxfind wants the bare hex; EPiServer's
# john form is two 0x-prefixed fields separated by a space; dynamic_1602 wraps
# hash and salt in "$dynamic_1602$...$...$$U<user>" and QAS-VASAUTH ignores the
# The WPA lines are a different KIND of transcode and are worth naming as such:
# they are not a reshuffle of one line's fields but a re-serialization of a
# binary struct. john stores a handshake as "$WPAPSK$<essid>#<475 chars>", where
# the tail is john's own base64 (the crypt "./0-9A-Za-z" alphabet, NOT RFC 4648)
# over the hccap_t of src/hccap.h; mdxfind and hashcat want hashcat's
# tools/wpapsk-transcode.pl does the decode, per the loop in john's src/wpapsk.h.
# These are hints about SPELLING, never claims. tools/attach-mdxfind-ahead.pl
# still has to see the line come back on stdout from `hashpipe -c` pinned to
# the named type, or nothing is written. A line here and the entry's stored
# vector are ONE piece of evidence written twice; the entry's note says so, so
# that a later reader does not count them as two agreeing vectors.
